source: NN/g four tone dimensions + 37 tone words + tone study, Mailchimp/Microsoft/Google style guides, reference works for comic and cultural registers; each item placed on the NN/g dimensions where a source supports it

items.name: Authoritative / expert
items.one_line: Confident, evidence-backed voice of someone who knows the subject and does not hedge without reason.

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g, Kate Moran)
sources.supports: 'Authoritative', 'Trustworthy' and 'Professional' are on NN/g's 37-word tone list used to plan and evaluate tone

sources.title: The Impact of Tone of Voice on Users' Brand Perception (NN/g)
sources.supports: in NN/g's study trustworthiness explained far more of desirability than friendliness did, so credibility is the job of this tone

items.note: NN/g dimensions: serious, respectful, leaning matter-of-fact; can be formal or casual (expert-but-conversational is common for creators).

items.name: Conversational
items.one_line: Writes the way a knowledgeable person talks: contractions, short everyday words, direct 'you'.

sources.title: The Impact of Tone of Voice on Users' Brand Perception (NN/g)
sources.supports: casual, conversational, moderately enthusiastic tones performed best in the NN/g tone study, even for banking

sources.title: Microsoft Style Guide: brand voice, above all simple and human
sources.supports: 'talk like a person': short everyday words, contractions, no jargon

sources.title: Google developer documentation style guide: voice and tone
sources.supports: conversational, friendly and respectful, like a knowledgeable friend; no slang or wackiness

items.note: NN/g dimensions: casual + serious (NN/g's 'conversational' sample was casual but serious). The safe default for most explainers, emails and captions.

items.name: Friendly / warm
items.one_line: Approachable and kind; reads like someone on the reader's side.

sources.title: Microsoft Style Guide: brand voice
sources.supports: voice principles 'warm and relaxed' and 'ready to lend a hand' (show customers you are on their side)

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Friendly', 'Caring', 'Cheerful' are NN/g tone words

sources.title: Mailchimp Content Style Guide: Voice and tone
sources.supports: 'genuine' voice trait; tone adjusted to the reader's emotional state

items.note: NN/g dimensions: casual, respectful, mildly enthusiastic. Friendliness alone did not drive desirability in the NN/g study; pair it with substance.

items.name: Playful / witty
items.one_line: Light, clever and fun; wordplay and surprise without losing the message.

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Samples (NN/g)
sources.supports: playful samples sit at funny + casual + irreverent + enthusiastic on the four dimensions

sources.title: The Impact of Tone of Voice on Users' Brand Perception (NN/g)
sources.supports: humorous copy hurt credibility in serious industries (study participants said friendliness took away credibility)

sources.title: Mailchimp Content Style Guide: Voice and tone
sources.supports: humour should come naturally; do not force jokes, keep a straight face when unsure; clarity beats entertainment

items.note: NN/g dimensions: funny, casual, irreverent-leaning, enthusiastic. Wrong for health, money-loss, grief or error states.

items.name: Irreverent / edgy
items.one_line: Pokes at conventions, authority or the category itself; deliberately not polite.

sources.title: The Four Dimensions of Tone of Voice (NN/g)
sources.supports: respectful vs irreverent is one of the four tone dimensions

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Irreverent', 'Edgy', 'Snarky', 'Unapologetic' and 'Coarse' are NN/g tone words

items.note: NN/g dimensions: irreverent pole, usually casual and funny. Target ideas and the category, never the reader.

items.name: Satirical (vyangya)
items.one_line: Exposes hypocrisy and folly through irony, exaggeration and mock-praise; the Hindi tradition is vyangya.

sources.title: Satire (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: satire ridicules vices and follies to criticise; Horatian (gentle) vs Juvenalian (scathing) distinction

sources.title: Harishankar Parsai (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: Parsai is the reference writer of Hindi vyangya: plain prose aimed at hypocrisy, corruption and pretence

items.note: Decide Horatian vs Juvenalian before writing. Satire needs a real target and a recognisable truth; political satire overlaps law/compliance (another worker's scope).

items.name: Sarcastic
items.one_line: Says the opposite of what it means to mock; cutting rather than gentle.

sources.title: Sarcasm (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: sarcasm is caustic, mocking use of words; it travels badly in text without vocal cues (RFC 1855 warning)

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Sarcastic' and 'Snarky' are NN/g tone words

items.note: NN/g dimensions: irreverent, funny. In text it needs context or markers or readers take it literally; risky in translation and captions.

items.name: Deadpan / dry
items.one_line: States absurd things flatly, with no visible emotion, and lets the reader find the joke.

sources.title: Deadpan (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: deadpan = deliberate emotional neutrality; humour comes from the contrast between flat delivery and absurd content

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Dry' and 'Matter-of-fact' are NN/g tone words

sources.title: Mailchimp Content Style Guide: Voice and tone
sources.supports: Mailchimp's voice uses dry humour rather than loud jokes

items.note: NN/g dimensions: funny but matter-of-fact (the opposite of hype). No exclamation marks, no emoji winks.

items.name: Technical / precise
items.one_line: Exact, unambiguous and consistent terminology; every sentence can be acted on.

sources.title: Google developer documentation style guide: voice and tone
sources.supports: knowledgeable-friend tone; avoid slang, jargon without need, figurative language, exclamation marks and over-politeness ('please' in steps)

items.note: NN/g dimensions: serious, matter-of-fact, respectful; casual-to-neutral formality. Simple consistent terms also help non-native readers and translation.

items.name: Hype / energetic creator
items.one_line: High-energy, exclamatory, excited voice that sells the moment.

sources.title: The Four Dimensions of Tone of Voice (NN/g)
sources.supports: matter-of-fact vs enthusiastic is a tone dimension; adding 'Oops!'-style exclamations raised perceived enthusiasm and casualness

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Enthusiastic', 'Upbeat' and 'Passionate' are NN/g tone words

sources.title: The Impact of Tone of Voice on Users' Brand Perception (NN/g)
sources.supports: moderate enthusiasm performed best; extreme playful samples cost credibility

items.note: NN/g dimensions: enthusiastic pole, casual. Keep it 'moderately enthusiastic' for trust; full hype only for launches, drops and reels.

items.name: Nostalgic
items.one_line: Evokes a shared past (childhood, a decade, old India) to create warmth and belonging.

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Nostalgic' is one of NN/g's 37 tone words

items.note: Works on specific sensory details of a period, not generic 'good old days'.

items.name: Bold / provocative
items.one_line: Takes a strong stand or challenges a belief head-on to start an argument.

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Provocative', 'Unapologetic' and 'Frank' are NN/g tone words

items.note: Can be serious (not only funny). The claim must be defensible; provocation without evidence reads as clickbait.

items.name: Academic / formal
items.one_line: Formal, impersonal, hedged and cited; claims sit inside existing evidence.

sources.title: Academic writing (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: formal tone, referencing other work, hedging between caution and certainty, compressed noun phrases

sources.title: The Four Dimensions of Tone of Voice (NN/g)
sources.supports: NN/g's formal example (Duke Health) sits at formal + serious + respectful + matter-of-fact

items.note: NN/g dimensions: formal, serious, respectful, matter-of-fact. Right for white papers, research summaries, government and institutional copy; too stiff for social.

items.name: Journalistic neutral
items.one_line: Reports what happened and who said what, from nobody's point of view; attribution over adjectives.

sources.title: Journalistic objectivity (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: objectivity = truthfulness, neutrality and detachment; known failure is false balance between unequal claims

items.note: NN/g dimensions (inferred, not stated by a source): serious, matter-of-fact, respectful, neutral formality. Neutral does not mean equal weight for a claim the evidence does not support. BBC impartiality guidelines were blocked to the fetcher; add them at card time if reachable.

items.name: Empathetic / supportive
items.one_line: Acknowledges how the reader feels before telling them what to do; patient, never jokey.

sources.title: Microsoft Style Guide: brand voice
sources.supports: voice stays constant while tone moves from serious to empathetic to lighthearted to fit the customer's state of mind

sources.title: NHS digital service manual: Voice and tone
sources.supports: tone adapts to anxious users; empowering not patronising; avoid jokey or flippant language in sensitive situations

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Sympathetic' and 'Caring' are NN/g tone words

items.note: NN/g dimensions: serious, respectful, casual-to-neutral, matter-of-fact. For grief, health, money loss, apologies and complaint replies.

items.name: Calm / reassuring
items.one_line: Steady, factual and quietly confident so an anxious reader feels safe to act.

sources.title: NHS digital service manual: Voice and tone
sources.supports: NHS voice combines authority with calm reassurance; balanced phrasing rather than alarm; avoid patronising 'should'

items.note: Use balanced facts (most people..., you can...) rather than 'don't worry'. Pairs with empathetic; differs from urgent.

items.name: Urgent
items.one_line: Direct, serious and action-first when time really matters: what to do, by when, why.

sources.title: NHS digital service manual: Voice and tone
sources.supports: for serious matters such as emergencies the NHS uses direct, serious and reassuring language

items.note: Real urgency only (deadline, safety, last date). Fake scarcity and countdown pressure are a compliance matter (another worker's kind); keep exclamation marks and caps out.

items.name: Inspirational / motivational
items.one_line: Optimistic and forward-looking; shows the reader what is possible and that they can get there.

sources.title: Atlassian Design System: Voice and tone
sources.supports: 'optimistic' voice trait; motivating by showing what is possible; optimism scaled to how sure the reader feels

sources.title: Jungian archetypes (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: the twelve branding archetypes (Mark and Pearson) include the Hero

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Passionate' and 'Upbeat' are NN/g tone words

items.note: NN/g dimensions: enthusiastic, serious-to-light, respectful. Anchor uplift in a concrete story or number, or it reads as poster-quote filler.

items.name: Luxury / premium
items.one_line: Restrained, assured and exclusive: craft, rarity and heritage, never discounts or shouting.

sources.title: Luxury goods (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: luxury brands communicate being top of their class; personalisation, special packaging and limited supply create exclusivity

items.note: Restraint (fewer adjectives, no exclamation marks, no 'cheap/offer') is common practice, not a sourced rule here; a luxury brand-voice source was not found within the search budget. Overlaps regal/heritage and minimalist.

items.name: Minimalist / understated
items.one_line: Fewest words, plain claims, white space; lets the product or fact speak.

sources.title: Microsoft Style Guide: brand voice
sources.supports: 'crisp and clear': bigger ideas, fewer words; prune every excess word; short sentences and fragments

sources.title: The Four Dimensions of Tone of Voice (NN/g)
sources.supports: matter-of-fact is the opposite pole to enthusiastic

items.note: NN/g dimensions: matter-of-fact, serious-to-dry, casual or formal. Understatement only works when the claim underneath is strong.

items.name: Corporate B2B professional
items.one_line: Clear, confident, practical business voice for buyers who need to justify a decision.

sources.title: Atlassian Design System: Voice and tone
sources.supports: a B2B voice built on bold, optimistic, practical-with-a-wink traits; tone scaled to the user's confidence and context

sources.title: The Impact of Tone of Voice on Users' Brand Perception (NN/g)
sources.supports: conversational beat cold formality even for financial services; trustworthiness drove desirability

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Professional', 'Conservative', 'Trustworthy' are NN/g tone words

items.note: NN/g dimensions: serious, respectful, matter-of-fact, casual-leaning per the study. Professional is not jargon: name outcomes, numbers and next steps.

items.name: Devotional / spiritual (bhakti)
items.one_line: Reverent, loving, surrendering voice addressed to or about a deity; the bhajan and katha register.

sources.title: Bhakti (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: bhakti = devotion, love and surrender to a deity; the movement used vernacular languages and poet-saints (Kabir, Tulsidas, Mirabai, Surdas); bhajan and kirtan forms

sources.title: Awadhi language (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas (1575) is the landmark devotional text, written in Awadhi

items.note: NN/g dimensions: serious, respectful, enthusiastic-to-calm. Never ironic; check scripture quotes against an edition (see lang:sanskrit_iast).

items.name: Gen-Z internet voice
items.one_line: Lower-case, meme-literate, in-group slang and self-aware irony, tuned to what is current this month.

sources.title: Internet slang (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: slang marks group belonging and spreads fast from creators to mainstream (e.g. 'rizz'; Dictionary.com's 2025 Word of the Year '67' from Gen Alpha TikTok)

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Trendy' and 'Quirky' are NN/g tone words

sources.title: Google developer documentation style guide: voice and tone
sources.supports: counter-rule: slang and internet abbreviations are avoided in documentation for global readers

items.note: NN/g dimensions: casual, funny, irreverent. Slang has a short half-life; verify any term is current before use, and never use it for docs, legal or support copy.

items.name: Storyteller / narrative
items.one_line: Carries the message inside a story: a character, a moment, a turn, a point of view.

sources.title: Storytelling (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: storytelling is increasingly used in advertising to build loyalty; core elements are plot, characters and narrative point of view

items.note: A voice, not a framework: tense, person and scene detail carry it. Story structures belong to the framework kind.

items.name: Tough-love coach
items.one_line: Frank, demanding and on the reader's side: names the excuse, then gives the next step.

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Frank' and 'Unapologetic' are NN/g tone words

items.note: NN/g dimensions: serious, casual, mildly irreverent, enthusiastic. Harsh on the behaviour, never on the person; always end with an action. Only the tone words are sourced; the coaching pattern is practice.

items.name: Inclusive
items.one_line: Bias-free wording that does not assume the reader's gender, ability, region or wealth.

sources.title: Microsoft Style Guide: Bias-free communication
sources.supports: gender-neutral terms (chair not chairman); no generic he/she; people-first disability language without pity words; diverse names and non-Western examples; no generalisations about cultures

items.note: A layer applied over any other tone. In Hindi, verb gender forces a choice; address the reader as aap and rephrase with plural or role nouns where possible.

items.name: Kid-friendly
items.one_line: Short, concrete, warm sentences a child can follow, without talking down.

sources.title: Netflix English (USA) Timed Text Style Guide
sources.supports: children's programmes get a slower reading speed (up to 17 characters per second vs 20 for adults)

sources.title: Google developer documentation style guide: voice and tone
sources.supports: avoid condescending phrasing

items.note: Children's advertising rules are a compliance matter for another worker. No scary urgency, no sarcasm (children read it literally).

items.name: Desi casual (Hinglish)
items.one_line: Easy Hindi-English mix with Indian references; sounds like a friend from the same city.

sources.title: Hinglish (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: Hinglish code-switching is common in Indian advertising and media; Google added Hinglish support to Gboard and Search

sources.title: Bali et al. 2014, 'I am borrowing ya mixing?' An Analysis of English-Hindi Code Mixing in Facebook
sources.supports: Hindi sentences carried English insertions far more often (23.7% of Hindi matrices) than English sentences carried Hindi (7.2%)

items.note: NN/g dimensions: casual, light, respectful-to-cheeky. Spelling and script rules are in lang:hinglish_roman and lang:hinglish_devanagari; this item is the attitude.

items.name: Regal / heritage
items.one_line: Stately, legacy-proud voice of an old house, a royal craft or a long tradition.

sources.title: Jungian archetypes (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: the Ruler is one of the twelve branding archetypes (Mark and Pearson, The Hero and the Outlaw)

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Conservative' and 'Nostalgic' are NN/g tone words

items.note: NN/g dimensions: formal, serious, respectful, matter-of-fact. Back the legacy with real dates and names; invented heritage is a false claim.

items.name: Data-driven / evidence-led
items.one_line: Leads with numbers, sources and tests; persuades by proof rather than adjectives.

sources.title: The Impact of Tone of Voice on Users' Brand Perception (NN/g)
sources.supports: trustworthiness, not friendliness, explained most of desirability in the study

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Informative', 'Smart' and 'Matter-of-fact' are NN/g tone words

items.note: NN/g dimensions: serious, matter-of-fact, respectful. Every number needs its source and date; one unsourced stat undoes the voice.

items.name: Humble / founder-candid
items.one_line: First-person, transparent, admits mistakes and shares real numbers.

sources.title: Buffer: Transparency
sources.supports: a named company practice (since 2013) of publishing finances, salaries and internal decisions to build trust

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Frank' is an NN/g tone word

items.note: NN/g dimensions: casual, serious, respectful, matter-of-fact. Candour needs specifics (what went wrong, the number); vague humility reads as a humblebrag.

items.name: Rebellious challenger brand
items.one_line: Names the category leader or the status quo as the enemy and positions the brand as the break-out.

sources.title: Jungian archetypes (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: the Outlaw is one of the twelve branding archetypes (Mark and Pearson, The Hero and the Outlaw)

sources.title: The Four Dimensions of Tone of Voice (NN/g)
sources.supports: respectful vs irreverent dimension

items.note: NN/g dimensions: irreverent, casual, enthusiastic. Comparative claims about named competitors are a compliance matter (another worker).

items.name: ASMR / soft
items.one_line: Hushed, slow, intimate voice for whisper VO, sleep, skincare and calm-down content.

sources.title: Autonomous sensory meridian response (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: ASMR triggers include whispering, soft speaking and personal attention; roughly 25 million ASMR videos on YouTube by 2022

items.note: Written for the ear: short phrases, sensory words, pauses marked in the script. Opposite of hype.

items.name: Romantic
items.one_line: Tender, intimate, longing voice for love, weddings, gifting and shayari-style captions.

sources.title: Tone-of-Voice Words (NN/g)
sources.supports: 'Romantic' is one of NN/g's 37 tone words

items.note: In Hindi this register leans on Urdu vocabulary (see lang:urdu_influenced_hindi).
